Requirement Statement: The firmware shall output the PWM signal on Arduino D7 (CN9 pin 8, MCU pin PA8).
Source Text / Evidence: Arduino D7 maps to CN9 pin 8 and MCU pin PA8.
Acceptance Criteria: Using a scope or logic analyzer, a PWM waveform is observable on Arduino D7 (CN9 pin 8 / PA8) during operation.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall configure PA8 in a timer alternate-function mode that supports PWM output (e.g., TIM1 Channel 1).
Source PRD Section: Pin and PWM Configuration (p. 1); Implementation Note (p. 2)
Source Text / Evidence:
PA8 shall be configured in an appropriate timer alternate-function mode for PWM output; TIM1 Channel 1 is the preferred implementation baseline.
The firmware shall therefore configure PA8 for a supported timer channel rather than treating D7 as GPIO-only.
Acceptance Criteria: Inspect MCU GPIO and timer configuration to confirm PA8 is set to a timer PWM alternate function (e.g., TIM1_CH1) and produces a PWM waveform.
Comments / Open Questions: TIM1 Channel 1 is stated as preferred, not mandatory; confirm whether any specific timer/channel is required for acceptance.

Requirement Statement: The PWM requirement shall refer to duty cycle on a 3.3 V MCU logic output and shall not imply a variable 5 V supply rail.
Source Text / Evidence: The D7 pin is a 3.3 V MCU logic output. The requirement refers to PWM duty cycle/effective output, not a variable 5 V supply rail.
Acceptance Criteria: By inspection of documentation and hardware, confirm the PWM is a 3.3 V logic-level output and no requirement exists to vary a 5 V rail via firmware.

Requirement Statement: The system shall not drive high‑power loads directly from the MCU pin; an external driver stage shall be used for loads exceeding GPIO electrical limits.
Source Text / Evidence: Do not connect a high‑power load directly to the MCU pin; use an external driver stage when controlling loads that exceed GPIO electrical limits.
Acceptance Criteria: Design documentation and test setup show any high‑power load is driven via an external driver and not directly from PA8.
Dependencies: ["External driver hardware when controlling higher‑power loads"]
Preconditions: Controlling a load that would exceed MCU GPIO limits.
Comments / Open Questions: Specify quantitative GPIO current/voltage/edge‑rate limits if they are to be enforced during verification.

Category: PWM Ramp State Machine & Runtime Execution
Requirement Statement: The firmware shall hold PA8 low (0% duty) whenever PWM generation is inactive, including during initialization and after any reset, until the PWM timer is configured and the initial 0% state is established.
Source Text / Evidence:
Start PWM generation automatically after board initialization.
Begin each cycle at 0% duty cycle.
Inference Rationale: Without forcing the output low before the timer is fully configured, PA8 can emit spurious pulses during bring-up, violating the requirement to begin at 0% and causing non-repeatable or unsafe behavior for attached low-power loads. Ensuring a defined inactive state is necessary to meet and verify the stated startup behavior.
Acceptance Criteria: From power-on/reset through entry into the first up-ramp, scope capture of PA8 shows a stable low level with no pulses prior to the start of PWM; the first active PWM state corresponds to a 0% duty cycle at cycle start.
Preconditions: Board reset or firmware about to initialize PWM.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Prior to enabling PWM, PA8 is low; the ramp then begins at 0% duty.
Failure Behavior: If PWM timer configuration/start fails, PA8 shall remain low and PWM generation shall not start until the next successful initialization or reset.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall not reconfigure PA8 or its alternate-function selection while PWM generation is active; the pin shall remain bound to the selected timer channel throughout operation.
Source PRD Section: Pin and PWM Configuration (p. 1); Implementation Note (p. 2)
Source Text / Evidence:
PA8 shall be configured in an appropriate timer alternate-function mode for PWM output; TIM1 Channel 1 is the preferred implementation baseline.
The firmware shall therefore configure PA8 for a supported timer channel rather than treating D7 as GPIO-only.
Inference Rationale: Reconfiguring PA8 during operation would interrupt or corrupt the PWM waveform, violating the requirements for constant carrier frequency and smooth continuous ramps, and undermining verification with a scope or logic analyzer.
Acceptance Criteria: While the ramp runs for at least one complete 10-second cycle, readings of GPIO/AF configuration before and after confirm PA8 remains mapped to the timer channel, and the observed waveform is continuous with no gaps or mode changes.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: PA8 remains in timer alternate-function mode for the entire operation.

Requirement Statement: Duty-cycle updates during each ramp shall be paced by a single monotonic timebase with a fixed update interval for the duration of the ramp.
Source Text / Evidence:
Avoid blocking delays that prevent normal firmware execution; duty-cycle updates should be timer/tick driven.
Up-ramp duration: 5.0 seconds.
Down-ramp duration: 5.0 seconds.
Ramp shape: linear with no intentional hold time at 0% or 100%.
Inference Rationale: A linear 5.0 s up-ramp and 5.0 s down-ramp cannot be achieved or verified if updates are driven by variable or blocking delays; a single monotonic scheduler with a fixed interval is necessary to maintain linearity and the specified durations.
Acceptance Criteria: During a ramp, timestamps collected for consecutive duty-cycle updates are strictly increasing and exhibit a constant interval equal to the implementation’s configured update period, with no missing updates due to blocking.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Update cadence remains fixed for the entire ramp.
Comments / Open Questions: No numeric jitter/tolerance is specified in the PRD; define acceptable update-interval variation if required for acceptance.

Category: PWM Ramp State Machine & Runtime Execution
Requirement Statement: The firmware shall clamp computed duty-cycle values to the valid range inclusive of the endpoints so the timer compare value never underflows below 0 or exceeds the auto-reload period, ensuring realizable 0% and 100% duty cycles.
Source Text / Evidence:
Duty-cycle endpoints: 0% and 100%.
Immediately reverse the ramp direction at 100% duty cycle.
Inference Rationale: Finite timer resolution and arithmetic rounding can produce values slightly outside [0%, 100%]; without clamping, compare values may wrap or overshoot, causing glitches or preventing true endpoint behavior, violating endpoint and reversal requirements.
Acceptance Criteria: Across both endpoints, inspection shows the timer compare register remains within [0, ARR]; when test logic attempts to push beyond the range, values are saturated and do not wrap; observed waveform is solid low at 0% and solid high at 100% with no extra edges.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: CCR values remain within valid bounds and endpoints are stable.

Requirement Statement: Duty-cycle updates shall not introduce extra PWM edges; during active operation each carrier period shall contain no more than one rising and one falling transition, except at 0% or 100% where the output is static.
Source PRD Section: Pin and PWM Configuration (p. 1); Verification and Acceptance Criteria (p. 2)
Source Text / Evidence:
Keep the PWM frequency fixed throughout the ramp.
PWM carrier frequency remains stable while the duty cycle ramps.
Inference Rationale: Multiple edges within a carrier period indicate frequency perturbations or update glitches that break the fixed-carrier assumption and undermine the linear, smooth ramp the PRD requires and intends to verify on a scope.
Acceptance Criteria: On an oscilloscope at carrier-period resolution, observe consecutive periods during duty-cycle updates; for each period there are at most two edges consistent with the carrier period and no additional narrow pulses appear during update instants.
Preconditions: PWM active and varying duty cycle.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Waveform shows one rising and one falling edge per period (except static endpoints).

Category: PWM Ramp State Machine & Runtime Execution
Requirement Statement: The firmware shall reverse ramp direction immediately at the duty‑cycle endpoints with no intentional hold time: upon reaching 100% the next update shall decrease duty cycle, and upon reaching 0% the next update shall increase duty cycle.
Source Text / Evidence:
Immediately reverse the ramp direction at 100% duty cycle.
Ramp shape: linear with no intentional hold time at 0% or 100%.
Acceptance Criteria: At both transition points (0% and 100%), the next duty‑cycle update changes ramp direction with no intentional dwell beyond the inherent update interval. Specifically: when the up‑ramp reaches 100%, the next update decreases duty cycle; when the down‑ramp reaches 0%, the next update increases duty cycle. Scope or logic‑analyzer captures around both endpoints show no plateau beyond a single update interval.
Preconditions: Ramp endpoint (0% or 100%) is reached during operation.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Ramp direction changes on the next update; no intentional dwell is present.
Comments / Open Questions: No maximum reversal latency/dwell is specified; define acceptable maximum dwell (e.g., one update interval) if needed for acceptance.
